methods.name: to_dict
methods.summary: Return the config as the JSON-ready dict `adapter_config.json` holds.
methods.extended:
Enums become their strings and sets of module names sorted lists,
so the result goes straight to `json.dumps` and back through
`from_dict`.  A field the reference's config of this method lacks
(`IA3Config.layers_to_transform`) is written only when it is set,
so a file that does not use it is one the reference reads too.

returns.description: One entry per field, keyed by the reference's field names.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> d = LoraConfig(target_modules=["v", "q"], task_type="CAUSAL_LM").to_dict()
>>> d["target_modules"], d["task_type"], d["peft_type"]
(['q', 'v'], 'CAUSAL_LM', 'LORA')

methods.name: from_dict
methods.summary: Build a config from a dict such as a parsed `adapter_config.json`.
methods.extended:
The constructor cannot do this: a file from the reference carries
keys v1 has no field for.  Such a key is accepted only at a value
that turns its feature off — null, false or empty
(`"loftq_config": {}`, `"megatron_config": null`) — and dropped (with
a warning if v1 does not know the key); at any other value it
raises, as it would change what the adapter computes.  The
`peft_version` provenance key is dropped.  Called on
`PeftConfig`, the dict's `peft_type` picks the class.

parameters.name: config_dict
parameters.description: The config's fields, by the reference's names.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class the dict's method names.

raises.description:
The dict describes another adapter type, or turns on a feature
v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig.from_dict(
...     {"peft_type": "LORA", "r": 4, "target_modules": ["c_attn"],
...      "use_dora": False, "loftq_config": {}, "peft_version": "0.17.0"})
>>> config.r, config.target_modules
(4, {'c_attn'})

members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with RandLoRA.
members.extended:
RandLoRA (Albert et al., 2025, [arXiv:2502.00987](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00987)) reaches a *full-rank* update
with few parameters: instead of one trainable low-rank pair it sums
$n = \lceil \min(d_{out}, d_{in}) / r \rceil$ frozen random rank-$r$
pairs $(B_i, A_i)$, drawn once and shared by every targeted layer, and
trains only a diagonal scale on each side,

$$
\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_i)\,A_i\,\mathrm{diag}(\gamma_i),
$$

with $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times n}$ and
$\gamma \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times \min(d_{out}, d_{in})}$ per layer.  Lowering
$r$ *raises* the number of trained parameters.  $\lambda$ starts at
zero, so the adapted model starts as the base; the update folds into the weight.

Names, order, defaults and the `adapter_config.json` layout follow the reference
adapter library.  `exclude_modules` is an addition
(it selects modules as `LoraConfig`'s does).

Seed of the generator the shared `randlora_A` / `randlora_B` are drawn

parameters.name: save_projection
parameters.description:
Write `randlora_A` / `randlora_B` into the adapter file.  `False` makes
the file small and redraws them from `projection_prng_key` on load (warns).

parameters.name: sparse
parameters.description:
Use ternary sparse bases (entries -1, 0, 1 with probabilities 1/6, 2/3, 1/6).
The bases are still dense tensors; the sparsity is not used for speed.

parameters.name: very_sparse
parameters.description: Use very sparse ternary bases (non-zero with probability $1/\sqrt{d_{min}}$).

parameters.name: randlora_dropout
parameters.description: Dropout on the update's input, in `[0, 1)`.

parameters.name: fan_in_fan_out
parameters.description:
For bases that store their weight `(in, out)`.  `nn.Linear` does not,
so `True` warns and is reset to `False`.

parameters.name: randlora_alpha
parameters.description: The update is scaled by `randlora_alpha / r` (typically 20 times the rank).

parameters.name: bias
parameters.description:
The reference also offers `"all"` and `"randlora_only"`; here the adapter
trains its own scales only, and those raise `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: modules_to_save
parameters.description: Modules trained in full beside the adapter (a classifier head).

parameters.name: init_weights
parameters.description:
`True`: $\lambda = 0$.  `False`: $\lambda \sim \mathcal N(0, 1)$
(the update is non-zero from the start — for tests).

parameters.name: layers_to_transform
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraConfig`.

parameters.name: layers_pattern
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraConfig`.

parameters.name: exclude_modules
parameters.description: Modules never adapted, matched like `target_modules`.

raises.description: A field has the wrong type (`projection_prng_key` is not an int, say).
`r` or another number is out of range.
`bias` asks for trained biases.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.randlora import RandLoraConfig
>>> config = RandLoraConfig(r=16, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"], randlora_alpha=320)
>>> sorted(config.target_modules), config.peft_type
(['q_proj', 'v_proj'], <PeftType.RANDLORA: 'RANDLORA'>)
>>> RandLoraConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True

members.summary: An `nn.Linear` with a RandLoRA update: $y = W x + b + \frac{\alpha}{r}\,\Delta\,\mathrm{drop}(x)$.

parameters.name: base_layer
parameters.description: The layer to adapt; the other parameters are those of `RandLoraLayer`.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter created at once.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.randlora import Linear, RandLoraConfig
>>> base = nn.Linear(8, 4)
>>> layer = Linear(base, "default", RandLoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["x"]))
>>> tuple(layer.randlora_lambda["default"].shape), tuple(layer.randlora_gamma["default"].shape)

>>> x = lucid.randn(2, 8)
>>> bool((layer(x) == base(x)).all().item())   # lambda starts at zero

methods.name: merge
methods.signature: merge(safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Fold the update into the base weights, in place.
methods.extended:
The weights keep their identity — they are written, not replaced —
so whatever holds them (an optimizer, a tied embedding) sees the
merged values.  That is also why a weight shared with another
module must not be merged into; the tuner's `merge_adapter` and
`merge_and_unload` refuse it, as this layer alone cannot see the
rest of the model.

found a non-finite merged weight.

(`lora_bias` on a base with no bias).
This layer's update cannot be written into its base weights.

methods.summary: Fold adapter updates into their base weights, keeping the adapter layers.

A merged model runs at the base model's cost; `unmerge_adapter`
takes the updates out again.  Every refusal is made before any
weight is written: nothing is merged if a layer's base weight is
shared with another module (a tied LM head — merging would change
that module too) or if the adapter is disabled.

methods.name: merge_and_unload
methods.signature: merge_and_unload(progressbar: bool = False, safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Merge the adapters into the base weights and return the plain model.
methods.extended:
Each adapter layer is replaced by its merged base module — the base
model's own module, holding its own `Parameter` objects — and each
`modules_to_save` entry by the active adapter's trained copy (the
original when that adapter has none).  Adapters not merged are
dropped with their layers.  Every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

`requires_grad` it had before injection.

members.summary: A model with RandLoRA layers put into it, the random bases they share, and the tools to take them out.
members.extended:
Construction replaces each `nn.Linear` `config` selects with a RandLoRA
layer around it and freezes every other parameter.  The model is changed in
place and kept as `model`; a public name this wrapper lacks is read from
it.  `config` itself is not changed: `peft_config` holds a copy with the
default `target_modules` spelled out.

The two random bases $A$ and $B$ are drawn once, sized for the
largest targeted layer, and held here as `randlora_A` / `randlora_B`
(tables of one tensor per adapter, aliased when adapters share them) — the
reference's attributes.  Every layer reads them from there; the first layer
holds them in its module tree, so a state dict lists each once and the adapter
file holds one pair.  Adapters added later must fit them (the same
`projection_prng_key`, `save_projection` and `r`, layer sizes no larger).

parameters.description: The model to adapt.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in every `randlora_lambda` / `randlora_gamma`.

parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

raises.description:
No module matches `target_modules`, a match is not an `nn.Linear`,
`modules_to_save` matches nothing, or an adapter does not fit the bases
of the first.
The model already holds adapter layers of another method.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.randlora import RandLoraConfig, RandLoraModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(8, 2))
>>> randlora = RandLoraModel(net, RandLoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0", "2"]), "default")
>>> tuple(randlora.randlora_A["default"].shape), tuple(randlora.randlora_B["default"].shape)
((2, 1, 8), (8, 4, 2))
>>> net[0].base_layer.weight.requires_grad, net[0].randlora_lambda["default"].requires_grad
(False, True)
>>> randlora.unload() is net, type(net[0]) is nn.Linear
(True, True)

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.randlora` — RandLoRA: a full-rank update from frozen random bases.
extended:
RandLoRA (Albert et al., 2025, [arXiv:2502.00987](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00987)) sums $n = \lceil\min(d_{out}, d_{in})/r\rceil$ frozen random rank-$r$ pairs $(B_i, A_i)$, shared by every adapted
layer, and trains only a diagonal scale on each side of each pair.  The update is full rank, yet the
trained parameters are scales; lowering `r` raises their number. Pick it when LoRA's rank is the
limit and the adapter must stay small.

Where the reference library keeps them, so `isinstance(m, RandLoraLayer)` and `from
lucid.peft.tuners.randlora import RandLoraConfig, Linear` read as they do there.  One layer type
for the one module the method adapts, `nn.Linear`.  `RandLoraConfig` and `RandLoraModel`
(which holds the shared bases) are here and exported from `lucid.peft`.  Importing the package
registers the method (its config under `PeftType.RANDLORA`, its tuner and layer), which is what
makes `get_peft_model` and `PeftModel.from_pretrained` know it.
citation: Albert, Paul, et al. "RandLoRA: Full-rank Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Models." [arXiv:2502.00987](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00987), 2025.
theory:
RandLoRA (Albert et al., 2025, [arXiv:2502.00987](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00987)) reaches a *full-rank* update
with few parameters: instead of one trainable low-rank pair it sums
$n = \lceil \min(d_{out}, d_{in}) / r \rceil$ frozen random rank-$r$
pairs $(B_i, A_i)$, drawn once and shared by every targeted layer, and
trains only a diagonal scale on each side,

$$
\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_i)\,A_i\,\mathrm{diag}(\gamma_i),
$$
